macro_cross_check.verdict: PROTEIN PASSES (-3.9%), so per rule 6 the portions are sound - no each-weight error exists (the protein is weight-anchored at 1 lb / 3 servings). The 116-cal gap is FAT, not portion: their 33 g fat vs our 20.2 g. Two identifiable, compatible explanations on their side: (a) fattier turkey - 85/15 raw carries ~8 g more fat per 151 g serving (~72 cal) than the house 93/7 booked here; (b) their figure counts the 'optional' sriracha mayo (+10 g fat, +88 cal), which their own step 8 applies without qualification. Either alone roughly closes the gap; both together overshoot slightly. Their carbs 15 vs our 9.2 likewise suggests they counted the pico/lettuce garnishes. Our recompute stands as the honest non-optional 93/7 build.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 360.1 cal in [400, 650] FAIL - 40 cal UNDER the floor. Carbs 9.2 g <= 35 PASS. Alternates for the gate's owner: counting the source-intended toppings gives ~463 cal (PASS); an 85/15 ground-turkey build gives ~432 cal without toppings (PASS) but has NO food-DB row (no verifiable 85/15 label on disk; rule 2 forbids inventing one). See loud_flags.

loud_flags: BAND FAIL AS MAPPED: 360 cal vs the 400 floor. This is a fat-class and topping-counting question, not a portion error (protein cross-check agrees within 4%). The in-run precedent for the identical generic phrase ('1 lb ground turkey' -> 93/7) was followed for consistency, but here the choice is decisive: the source's own fat figure implies 85/15 turkey and/or counted toppings. THREE honest paths, none of them mine to rule: (1) capture a real 85/15 ground-turkey label (meal-macro lane / Brad) and re-map to the generic ground-turkey commodity (7 of 7, $2.6633/lb - CHEAPER than 93/7, and arguably the truer generic-term match) -> ~432 cal PASS; (2) promote the source's step-8 toppings from optional -> ~463 cal PASS; (3) reject the recipe at the gate. Parking this decision in QA rather than silently fudging a row.

board_defects_observed: Term 'cauliflower rice' resolves to the RICE commodity (include /\brice\b/) - a false product-concept match (white rice is not cauliflower); the cauliflower commodity's include /cauliflower/ also claims the sibling phrasings 'riced cauliflower' and 'frozen cauliflower', so resolver priority hands the worse answer to the most common phrasing. Flagged for the match-soundness gate.

Shallots price-routing split: ingredient-map (and the standing Brad ruling) route Shallots -> onions ($0.7967/lb class) while a live shallots commodity prices 4 of 7 at $3.99/lb. If variety pricing is meant to govern (red-onion precedent), the standing ruling deserves a re-look; recorded, not changed.
